sentences.text: Dated this the 16th day of January, 2024  ORDER
Petitioner has invoked the jurisdiction under Section 482 Cr.P.C to quash all proceedings against him.

2. Petitioner is the accused in C.C. No.48 of 2023 on the files of the Chief Judicial Magistrate's Court, Thiruvananthapuram, arising out of Crime No.696 of 2014 of Nemom Police Station,
Thiruvananthapuram, registered for the offence under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 apart from Section 13 r/w Section 17 of the Kerala Money Lenders Act, 1958 and Sections 3 and 4 of Raju vs State Of Kerala on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132876075/
2 the Prize Chits and Money Circulation (Banning Act), 1978.

entities.text: Prize Chits and Money Circulation (Banning Act), 1978
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Respondents 2 to 6 are the defacto complainants.

3. According to the prosecution, petitioner conducted money lending business during the period from 2007 till 2014, without authority and indulged in money circulation schemes and thereby committed the offences alleged.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned counsel for the respondent, apart from the learned Public Prosecutor.
5.
The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the matter has been settled and hence the proceedings against the petitioner ought to be quashed.
It was also submitted that, considering the nature of CRL.MC NO. 11019 OF 2023 offences alleged, no purpose would be served by continuing the proceedings.

6. In Gian Singh v. State of Punjab and Another [(2012) 10 SCC 303], the Apex Court has held that in appropriate cases, the High Court can take note of the amicable resolution of disputes between the victim and the wrongdoer to put an end to the criminal proceedings.

entities.text: Gian Singh v. State of Punjab and Another [(2012) 10 SCC 303]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This view was reiterated in Narinder Singh and Others v. State of Punjab and Another [(2014) 6 SCC 466] and Yogendra Yadav and Others v. State of Jharkhand and Another [(2014) 9 SCC 653].
7.

entities.text: Narinder Singh and Others v. State of Punjab and Another [(2014) 6 SCC 466]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Yogendra Yadav and Others v. State of Jharkhand and Another [(2014) 9 SCC 653]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have perused A2 to A6 affidavits filed by respondents 2 to 6.
The learned Public Prosecutor has submitted that upon verification, it is understood that the affidavits are genuine, and the defacto complainants stand by the contents thereof.
I am satisfied that the matter has been settled and no public interest is involved in this case.
There is no impediment for granting the prayer for quashing.
The continuance of the proceedings will only be an exercise in futility.

8. In the decision in Gold Quest International Pvt. Ltd. v.State of Tamil Nadu and Others [(2014) 15 SCC 235], the Supreme Court had quashed the cases that implicated the accused for the offences under the Prize Chits and Money Circulation (Banning Act), 1978 after noticing that the monetary disputes had been settled and the sufferers had entered into an agreement with the appellant to settle the claims.

entities.text: Gold Quest International Pvt. Ltd. v.State of Tamil Nadu and Others [(2014) 15 SCC 235]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Prize Chits and Money Circulation (Banning Act), 1978
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 9. Since the aggrieved persons have filed affidavits stating that the CRL.MC NO. 11019 OF 2023 entire disputes between them and their money claims have been settled, no purpose would be achieved by continuing the prosecution.
10. Accordingly, all proceedings against the petitioner in C.C. No.48 of 2023 on the files of the Chief Judicial Magistrate's Court, Thiruvananthapuram are quashed.
This Crl.M.C is allowed as above.
